overview: Briscoe Group is a New Zealand dual-format specialty retailer operating the Briscoes Homeware chain (47 stores) and Rebel Sport (43 stores) across New Zealand, plus a single Auckland distribution centre and support centre. The Group sells homewares, appliances and sporting goods through bricks-and-mortar stores (over 80% of sales) and a growing online/direct-to-customer channel (~20% of sales), and separately holds a passive minority equity stake (~3.3-6.75%, diluted through the year) in ASX/NZX-listed KMD Brands (Kathmandu). Founder and Managing Director Rod Duke, who acquired the business in 1990, remains the controlling shareholder (~77-81%) and chief executive.

business_model.summary: Briscoe Group is a value-oriented, promotion-led retailer that buys internationally sourced homeware and sporting goods and sells them through owned stores and online channels in New Zealand only. Revenue is transactional (single-purchase retail), not recurring/subscription, with sales seasonally weighted to the pre-Christmas and winter promotional periods. Same-day/omnichannel fulfilment and loyalty programmes (Club Briscoes, Rebel Sport rewards) support repeat purchase behaviour, but the core model is discount/promotional retail rather than contracted recurring revenue.
business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market and value-conscious New Zealand consumers; single-country geographic footprint (no international stores)
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% New Zealand (Briscoes Homeware and Rebel Sport stores nationwide); KMD Brands equity stake provides indirect, non-operating exposure to Kathmandu/Rip Curl/Oboz which are internationally diversified

main_competitors: Rebel/BCF equivalents and independent sporting goods retailers
competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest dedicated homeware and sporting goods retailers in New Zealand; consistently one of the most profitable listed NZ retailers with a debt-free balance sheet, positioned in the mid-market value/promotional segment rather than premium or deep-discount

moat_factors.description: National store network and volume purchasing from international suppliers support competitive sourcing costs versus smaller independents
Homeware and sporting goods exposures partially offset each other (e.g., sport benefiting from major events while homeware is housing-cycle sensitive)
No external term debt and $130m+ cash allow investment through the cycle (Drury DC) while competitors (e.g., The Warehouse Group) have struggled with profitability and leverage

moat_factors.factor: Store network density and brand recognition
moat_factors.description: Long-established, well-known brands (since 1990s) with loyal customer base and high in-store NPS scores
Aggressive, disciplined promotional cadence historically wins share versus Farmers and Warehouse on perceived value

weaknesses: Single-country concentration (100% New Zealand) with no geographic diversification to buffer a domestic downturn
High customer concentration risk on discretionary categories (homeware/sport) most exposed to consumer confidence and housing market cycles
Gross margin under structural pressure from competitive/promotional intensity (down from ~45.8% in 2021 to 39.2% in FY2026)
Small-cap, tightly-held stock (Rod Duke ~77-81%) with thin free float and limited independent board renewal visibility

Non-core KMD Brands equity stake has been a source of volatility/dilution (diluted from 6.75% to ~3.3% via KMD's discounted capital raise, and a lost dividend stream) without operational control or synergies

growth_drivers: New North Island distribution centre at Drury - largest capital investment in company history, targeting improved inventory flow, on-shelf availability, replenishment frequency and, over time, margin/productivity gains; practical completion expected April/May 2026 with automation ramp-up through late 2026
Online and direct-to-customer growth - online sales reached ~20% of Group sales (first time above 20% post-COVID), supported by new Adobe Commerce platform and Marketplacer marketplace launch
Rebel X flagship concept store (Mt Wellington) - new store format benchmark for sports retail in Australasia; positive early customer/supplier reception, being evaluated for further rollout
Merchandise planning and analytics uplift (Impact Analytics modules) - aimed at improving range execution, promotional effectiveness and inventory discipline to help repair gross margin
SAP S/4HANA ERP migration and broader technology/AI investment - scalability and efficiency platform for the next phase of growth
Store refurbishment programme (Westgate, Henderson, Wellington CBD) - modernising format mix and unlocking productivity per square metre
Potential normalisation of NZ consumer confidence, interest rates and housing market providing cyclical tailwind to currently-suppressed homeware demand
Exploration of new business opportunities/partnerships to extend addressable market beyond the core two-brand, single-market model (early-stage, per FY2024-27 strategic plan)

business.description: Sustained gross margin compression (down ~600bps since 2021) driven by highly value-driven, promotional competitive environment among Warehouse, Kmart, Farmers and online entrants
Homeware sales are directly linked to housing market activity (turnover, renovations) which has been weak; both brands sell non-essential discretionary goods vulnerable to squeezed household budgets

business.risk: Execution risk on Drury DC / ERP transition
business.description: Large, multi-year, multi-phase capital programme (new DC, automation, WMS, SAP S/4HANA) carries integration and go-live risk; benefits are not expected to materially flow through until late 2026 and beyond
100% New Zealand revenue base offers no geographic diversification if the domestic economy underperforms

Illiquid/volatile minority stake in a turnaround retailer (Kathmandu/Rip Curl/Oboz) with no board control; diluted via a deeply discounted capital raise BGP chose not to participate in, and cut its dividend income to zero in FY2026

financial.risk: Elevated capex through the investment cycle
financial.description: A further ~$57m of capex anticipated in FY2027 as the Drury DC completes; a new $30m trade finance facility was established (undrawn at FY2026 balance date, expected drawdown from April 2026), modestly increasing financial leverage during the build phase
Interest income fell to $3.0m (from $6.1m) as cash balances are drawn down to fund the capital programme and rates ease
FY2026 total dividend cut to 20.0 cps from 22.5 cps in FY2025, reflecting lower NPAT; payout policy (60%+ of NPAT) means further profit softness could pressure dividends further

regulatory.description: General exposure to NZ consumer protection, employment law and import/tariff settings; no major pending NZ-specific regulatory threats identified in filings
Group is building out mandatory climate-related disclosures (NZ CRD regime) and Scope 3 emissions capability, an incremental compliance cost

macro.risk: NZ consumer confidence and discretionary spending
macro.description: Persistent pressure on consumer sentiment and real (inflation-adjusted) sales volumes; management explicitly flagged a challenging, uncertain near-term operating environment
Homeware demand tied to housing transaction volumes and renovation activity, both depressed by higher-for-longer NZ interest rates through 2024-2026

macro.risk: Freight, fuel and import cost volatility
macro.description: Management flagged that global developments (geopolitical, tariffs) could reintroduce volatility to fuel prices and freight costs, flowing through to operating costs and household budgets
Predominantly internationally sourced product ranges expose margins to NZD movements against USD/other sourcing currencies

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ discretionary retail remains under pressure from weak consumer confidence and a soft housing market, though there are early signals of easing inflation and lower interest rates; a sustained recovery in consumer spending has yet to clearly materialise as of mid-2026
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - both Briscoes Homeware (housing cycle) and Rebel Sport (discretionary spend, partially offset by major sporting events) are cyclical, discretionary retail categories
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-high indirect sensitivity via NZ consumer discretionary spending and housing market activity; direct balance sheet sensitivity currently low given no term debt, though a new trade finance facility increases this modestly
key_input_costs: Internationally sourced homeware and sporting goods (landed cost/FX)

recent_developments.event: Q2 FY2027 (quarter to 27 July 2026) trading update: Group sales up only 0.25% to $192.9m; Rebel Sport +4.84% (boosted by Commonwealth Games/football World Cup-related demand) while Briscoes Homeware fell 2.17% on milder winter weather and constrained discretionary spend; half-year NPAT guided to not less than $27m, ~8% below prior year's $29.31m despite higher sales; gross margin forecast to fall a further ~57bps (an improvement on the prior year's 115bps decline)

FY2026 full-year results (52 weeks to 25 January 2026): record Group sales of $798.8m (+0.93%), but NPAT fell 2.3% to $59.2m (from $60.6m) on gross margin compression (39.23% vs 40.37% prior year); final dividend 10.0 cps, full-year dividend cut to 20.0 cps from 22.5 cps; balance sheet remained debt-free with $130.3m cash

Rebel X flagship concept store opened at Mt Wellington (transformed existing Rebel Sport store) - new benchmark format for sports retail in Australasia, described as receiving strongly positive customer/supplier feedback
Mark Cairns appointed Independent Non-Executive Director (effective 1 November 2025), bringing logistics/supply-chain/capital markets experience relevant to the Drury DC programme

KMD Brands completed a heavily discounted capital raise; Briscoe Group elected not to participate, diluting its stake from ~6.75% to ~3.3% and causing it to fall below the substantial-shareholder disclosure threshold; KMD also paid no dividend during the year (vs $2.9m pre-tax received the prior year), a modest drag on Group NPAT

Construction of the new North Island distribution centre at Drury progressing on schedule and within budget; building handover expected late April 2026, manual operations from end April 2026, automation installation targeted September 2026 with volume ramp-up in Q4 2026
Board renewal: Chair Dame Rosanne Meo will not seek re-election at the May 2027 AGM; director Andy Coupe retires at the May 2026 AGM after almost 10 years on the board
Group confirmed migration to SAP S/4HANA ERP platform and continued platform upgrades (Adobe Commerce, Marketplacer) as part of the technology transformation strategy

items.metric: Half-year (H1 FY2027) Net Profit After Tax
items.notes: Approximately 8% below prior year's $29.31m despite sales growth, reflecting continued gross margin compression

items.target: further decline of approximately 57 basis points
items.notes: Compares favourably with the 115bps decline in the prior comparable half; management continues to target a return to positive margin growth in FY2026/27 (per FY2026 annual report commentary)

items.vs_prior: reduced vs FY2026 ($49.1m PP&E + $1.3m intangibles = $50.4m actual investing spend in FY2026, prior year $58.2m)
items.notes: Predominantly relates to completion of the Drury distribution centre construction, fit-out and automation programme

items.target: practical completion end April 2026; automation build completed end September 2026; automation volume ramp-up in Q4 2026
items.vs_prior: on schedule and within budget, maintained
items.notes: Benefits (improved inventory flow, availability, margin) expected to begin emerging toward the end of 2026 with increasing flow-through thereafter

items.target: payout of at least 60% of full-year NPAT
items.vs_prior: maintained (policy unchanged; FY2026 absolute dividend cut reflects lower profit, not a policy shift)
items.notes: Board balancing shareholder returns against funding capacity for the major investment programme

guidance.management_commentary: Managing Director Rod Duke noted a third consecutive quarter of positive sales growth despite challenging economic conditions, but flagged real (inflation-adjusted) sales volumes are still contracting. Management expects the operating environment to remain uncertain near-term, with early signs of easing inflation and lower interest rates not yet translating into stronger consumer confidence; competitive intensity remains high. The Christmas trading quarter is flagged as critical to the full FY2027 outcome. Management reiterated confidence that the combination of a strong customer proposition, disciplined execution, and the upgraded supply-chain/technology platform (Drury DC, SAP S/4HANA, Adobe/Marketplacer, Impact Analytics) positions the Group to grow market share and improve profitability as conditions normalise over the next three to four years, with the current year marking the transition from an investment phase to a value-delivery phase.

bull_case: Debt-free balance sheet with $130m+ cash provides resilience and optionality that many NZ retail peers (e.g., The Warehouse Group) lack, allowing Briscoe to keep investing and take share through the downturn

Multi-year Drury distribution centre and technology transformation programme (WMS, automation, SAP S/4HANA, Adobe Commerce/Marketplacer, Impact Analytics) is nearing completion and is expected to structurally lift margin, availability and productivity from late 2026 onward
Record sales achieved even in a weak consumer environment, with online penetration crossing 20% of sales for the first time post-COVID, evidencing brand strength and omnichannel execution
Rebel Sport's exposure to major sporting events (Commonwealth Games, football World Cup) and the new Rebel X flagship format provide a growth lever partially offsetting soft homeware demand
Any recovery in NZ consumer confidence, interest rates or the housing market would be a strong cyclical tailwind given Briscoe's high operating leverage to volume/margin recovery
bear_case: Gross margin has structurally eroded from ~45.8% (2021) to ~39.2% (FY2026) amid intense promotional competition, and management's own guidance still points to further (if slowing) margin decline in H1 FY2027
100% New Zealand, discretionary-goods concentration leaves the Group fully exposed to a prolonged domestic consumer/housing downturn with no geographic diversification

Large, multi-year capital programme (Drury DC, automation, ERP) carries execution risk and near-term negative operating leverage before benefits materialize, with a new trade finance facility signaling increased reliance on external funding during the build phase
Dividend was cut in FY2026 (20.0 cps vs 22.5 cps) and further NPAT softness (H1 FY2027 guided down ~8%) could pressure payouts further given the 60%-of-NPAT policy

Extremely concentrated, closely-held share register (Rod Duke ~77-81%) limits free float/liquidity and raises long-term key-person/succession considerations, alongside an upcoming Chair transition (Dame Rosanne Meo stepping down 2027)
